clue.text: Coffee houses inferior to European shop that's cleaner

indicators.note: houses means holds within, so the coffee word surrounds the following pieces

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
inferior means lower, below, i.e. under

explanation.surface: A café chain seems to rank below a European shop with cleaner premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coffee houses' looks like a noun phrase for cafés; 'houses' is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service laundry is a shop where clothes are washed, so it is literally a cleaner's shop.

clue.text: A factor for marketing product with diamonds shows future promise

parts.note: a USP, unique selling point, is the feature used to market a product
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A marketing angle for selling jewellery shows signs of a bright future.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen or portent, a sign of things to come, often a favourable one.

clue.text: Part of goal went well, made some business contacts

parts.note: the net is part of a football goal
worked means succeeded, went well

explanation.surface: A footballer whose goal came off well afterwards met some sponsors.
explanation.definitionFit: To network is to build professional connections, so the past tense means having made such contacts.

clue.text: Half-heartedly waver to lift part of the body

indicators.note: to lift means raising, reading upwards in this down entry
half-heartedly means losing half of the doubled middle letters, so one of the pair at its heart goes

parts.note: to wobble is to waver

explanation.surface: Someone wavering half-heartedly as they raise a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: WOBBLE loses one B from its centre to give WOBLE, which reads upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint midway along the arm is a body part, used for nudging.

clue.text: Tongue's no good in chutney that's dispensed with starter

indicators.note: in means the abbreviations sit inside the shortened chutney word
dispensed with starter means its first letter is dropped

parts.note: relish is a chutney-style condiment

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek verdict that the chutney is no good once the starter is skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' is a language here, not food, despite the chutney and starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language, and this is the language of Britain and much of the world.

clue.text: Uneasiness after former girlfriend's moved out of annexe

indicators.note: moved out of means leaving, so the ex letters are removed from the building word

parts.note: an extension is an annexe added to a building
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Tension in the household now that the ex-girlfriend has moved out of the granny flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is nervous strain, a state of unease or stress.

clue.text: Swimmer the French caught in three seconds

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the French article sits within the seconds

parts.note: three words for a second run together: S, its abbreviation; tick, a moment; and back, to second or support someone
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A swimmer caught in a fraction of a second by a French timekeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The stickleback is a small spiny fish, which is a natural swimmer.

clue.text: Nothing in dirty sinks stored in vessel

indicators.note: sinks means moves lower, which in this down entry means further along

parts.note: soiled means dirty
O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing in the dirty sinks was put away in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinks' looks like kitchen basins but is a verb: the O moves down two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain kept in a silo, a storage tower, has been stored in that vessel.

clue.text: Clothing initially tight, actress wanting large

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word tight
wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the actress's name

parts.note: Kate Winslet is the English actress of Titanic
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A tight outfit on a film actress who has slimmed down from a large size.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching jumper-and-cardigan set worn by women is a classic item of knitwear, hence clothing.

clue.text: Former suggestion to take alcohol confines good bridge players

indicators.note: confines means holds in, so the drink-invitation letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: BYO, bring your own, is the note on an invitation suggesting guests take their own drink

explanation.surface: An old hint to bring a bottle keeps a good bridge pairing together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bygone belongs to the past, so it is an adjective synonym for erstwhile or past.

clue.text: Neither compiler nor solver could be murderer

definitions.text: Neither compiler nor solver could be murderer

parts.words: Neither compiler nor solver could be murderer
parts.note: the setter is the first person (I) and the solver the second (you); the someone else of grammar, and a murder-mystery's unknown other party, is neither

explanation.surface: A whodunit where the setter and solver are both cleared of the murder.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'I' or 'me' and address solvers as 'you', the first and second grammatical persons.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the pronouns he, she and they form the person after I and you, an outsider to both.

clue.text: Food from Australia one brought back after unpleasant job finished early

indicators.note: after means the reversed pieces come behind the shortened job in the answer
finished early means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a chore is a tedious or unpleasant task

indicators.note: brought back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone brings food back from Australia after cutting short a nasty job.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a spicy Spanish pork sausage, an example of a food.

clue.text: Desire to eat whipped cream?

definitions.note: cream as a colour adjective, an off-white shade; the question mark flags a definition by example

indicators.note: to eat means to take in, so the desire word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a wish is a desire
whipped means struck, i.e. hit

explanation.surface: A longing to tuck into some whipped cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped cream' reads as a dessert, but 'whipped' is a past tense verb and 'cream' is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is a pale yellowish-white colour, one shade that could be described as nearly white.

clue.text: Rat messing with this animal home might make dog alert

indicators.note: messing with means jumbling together, so the rat letters plus the answer's letters are rearranged into the final phrase

explanation.surface: A rat interfering with an animal's home might put the guard dog on alert.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of RAT plus the answer, shuffled, give DOG ALERT; 'might make' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaver's or otter's den is called by this word, so it is an animal's dwelling place.

clue.text: Old campaigner supplies cash, saving a southern revolutionary Frenchman

parts.note: kit means equipment or supplies

indicators.note: saving means except for, so the named letters are taken out of the cash word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: An old soldier provides funds while keeping back some for a French revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' looks like keeping money, but it means 'except'. Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal and war minister famous from the First World War recruiting poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchener led military campaigns in Sudan and South Africa, so he is a historic campaigner.

clue.text: Oppressive temperature year upon year around Ohio

indicators.note: upon means sitting on top of, so the first year comes before the second in the down entry
around means surrounding, so the Latin year encloses the next letter

parts.note: annus is Latin for year

explanation.surface: Year after year of oppressive temperatures around Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules harshly, so tyrannous means cruel and oppressive.

clue.text: Party in essence fuelling drinker's spree?

definitions.text: Party in essence fuelling drinker's spree?

indicators.note: fuelling means feeding into, so the core letters go inside the spree word

parts.note: a bender is a drinking binge

indicators.note: in essence points to the heart of the word party, its letters without the ends

explanation.surface: A party, at its core, is what keeps a drinking binge going.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also defines: the person serving drinks is the one who fuels a binge, with the question mark flagging the playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: The person behind the bar pours the drinks, so he or she literally keeps a boozer's spree supplied.

clue.text: One who delivers letters in secure jar before king

indicators.note: before means the jumbled letters come ahead of the king's letter
jar means jolt or shake, so the letters of secure are jumbled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A postman with letters secured in a jar ahead of the king's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who delivers' suggests a postman, given 'letters'; it means a saviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to save them from danger, so a deliverer is a saviour.

clue.text: Joy about having switched over current account previously

indicators.note: previously means coming earlier, so the reversed pieces go before the about word
switched over means turned the other way round, so those letters run backwards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a tale is an account or story
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Joy at having switched over a current account earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current account' reads as banking, but 'current' is I and 'account' is TALE; together reversed they give ELATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is intense happiness, a feeling of great joy.

clue.text: Refill vessel that's turned over

parts.note: a pot is a cooking or drinking vessel

explanation.surface: Filling up a container again once it has been tipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: To refill a glass or a phone's credit is to replenish it, the same as the hyphenated verb.

clue.text: Bird I trapped in net chewed cable

indicators.note: trapped in means caught inside, so the bird and I go within the jumbled net
chewed means mangled, so the letters of net are rearranged

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.definitionFit: A towline is the rope or cable used for towing a vehicle or boat.

clue.text: Satellite's lead going round house, well set up

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the lead symbol encloses the house abbreviation

explanation.definitionFit: Phobos is one of the two small moons of Mars, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Article on group from south Indian state

explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Wealthy people no longer on power trips

clue.text: Around university, see you making recordings

clue.text: River banks in Cork and Linz eroded by ducks over a century

indicators.note: banks in points to the edges of the two city names, which are then worn away
